messages.subject: Prediction
parts:
Hi,

 

I would like to know if it is possible to perform prediction in unobserved locations using only the spatial component in the model (without covariates). For example, I would like to identify areas of higher marine mammal by-catch in southern Brazil. In this case the response variable would be presence/absence of marine mammal by-catch in gillnet fishery.

 

 Thank you,

 

Jonatas Prado

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Prediction
parts:
Hi Jonatas,

You can do, however you need to have data (enough) around (the uncertainty is usually bigger near corners). Sometimes, you have to consider if the uncertainty in the prediction is not too big.

Consider the example:
  n <- 100
  y <- rbinom(n, 1, 1/(1+exp(-2*sin(2*pi*1:n/n))))
  y[c(1:10, 60:70)] <- NA ### no data at some places

 require(INLA)

 res1 <- inla(y ~ f(i, model='rw1'), ### less smooth
    family='binomial', data=list(y=y, i=1:n),
   control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE, link=1))
   plot(res1, F, F, F, F, T)

  res2 <- inla(y ~ f(i, model='rw2'), ### smoother
    family='binomial', data=list(y=y, i=1:n),
   control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE, link=1))
  plot(res2, F, F, F, F, T)

In this example you can have some feeling about prediction uncertainties and smoothness.

Elias
